name: linked-single-unit-average-write
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The required multi-destination constants declare one float source at table element zero and one active float destination at element one, so the small-parameter average path executes only its unit window and bounded single-lane collective before writing exact one.

name: imageblock-neighbours-and-extent-of-an-executed-command-template
rationale: The compute template of executed commands whose imageblock size a kernel encodes (DESIGN D336), run as its own case: 8 x 2 threads in threadgroups of 4 x 2 with an explicit imageblock of 4 x 2. Each thread stages 0x10000 | lid.x | lid.y << 8 in its cell, then reads its right-hand neighbour's, wrapping at the threadgroup's width: out[gid.y * 8 + gid.x] = (0x10000 | ((lid.x + 1) % 4) | lid.y << 8, 4, 2, gid.x | gid.y << 8).

name: let-lanes-zero-and-three-decide-the-block-edge-for-all-four
rationale: ExtraInloopDeblockH gives each thread one texture column and decides, for every aligned group of four columns, whether that block edge is filtered -- and it reaches the other columns' measurements with nothing but two simdgroup shuffles. Each lane measures its own second difference across the edge, air.simd_shuffle_down.s.i32 with delta 3 adds lane L+3's measurement to lane L's, and air.simd_shuffle.s.i32 with lane (simdLaneID & ~3) hands lane 4k's sum to all four lanes of the group; the same pair carries the strong-filter vote, where the shuffle_down is an AND so the group filters strongly only if lanes 4k and 4k+3 both vote for it. The 32 columns are eight independent groups and every one of them is arranged so a lane that read its own measurement instead of the group's would take a different branch. Group 0 skips because lane 3 alone is the spiky column: lanes 0, 1 and 2 are smooth ramps that would each filter on their own, and they come out byte-identical to their input. Group 1 filters strongly on the votes of lanes 0 and 3 while lanes 1 and 2, whose p0/q0 step is far past (5*tc+1)/2, vote against it and are filtered anyway -- lane 5's p0 lands on the p0 +/- 2*tc clamp. Group 7 is the converse and pins the AND: lanes 0, 1 and 2 all vote strong and lane 3 does not, so the whole group takes the weak path instead. The middle five groups walk the weak filter: group 2 adjusts both p1 and q1, group 3 holds q1 because d1 crosses (beta + beta/2)/8, group 4 holds p1 for the mirror reason, group 5 holds both and moves only p0 and q0, and in group 6 the two interior lanes have a delta past 10*tc and return untouched between two lanes that do filter. Groups 2 and 6 also carry interior columns whose own second difference is two hundred, which is past beta, so they would skip entirely if the broadcast were missing. The second component of every texel repeats the next group's first component, so each of the eight blocks exercises two different branch combinations, and every arithmetic result stays a small exact integer. The texture is eight rows tall, which is the shortest height that enters the row loop at all and leaves it after one pass, so the kernel writes p2, p1, p0 and q0 from the loop body and flushes q1 and q2 from the tail. Rows 0 and 7 are never written and keep their initial bytes; the third and fourth components start at distinct non-zero values everywhere and the kernel zeroes them on exactly the six rows it writes.

name: a-blit-shifts-by-a-function-constant-and-truncates
rationale:
A `texture2d<ushort, write>` written from a vector whose upper three lanes are `undef`. Building that texel means asking what type each lane's value has, and the answer can live in the pass's own PENDING instruction list rather than in the module -- `images::write_read::pending_or_module_result_type` looks there first and falls back to the module. Nine corpus sources reach it and no authored case did; measured with per-function coverage against every cased source, this host reaches it and it is the only unverified function it reaches.

The kernel is a luma blit under two required function constants. `kBitDepth` is authored 10, and the module's static initializer turns that into a pixel shift of 16 - 10 = 6 -- the `== 8` arm would give 0 -- so each thread writes `(ushort)(src[gid].x << 6)`. That constant is what the nine source texels are chosen to measure, because the shift is done in 32 bits and TRUNCATED back to 16: 1024, 2048, 4096 and 32768 all shift clean out of the sixteen bits and answer 0, 65535 answers 65472, 12345 answers 3648, and 1, 2 and 4 answer 64, 128 and 256. A shift folded to 0 (the other `kBitDepth` arm, or a function constant that never reached the module) leaves all nine equal to their source; a shift done in 16 bits, or a truncation that saturated instead of wrapping, moves a different subset of the nine.

`kNonUniformDispatch` is authored 0, which is the arm that KEEPS the module's bounds check -- each thread compares its gid against `air.get_width_texture_2d`/`air.get_height_texture_2d` of the DESTINATION and returns without writing if it is outside. Every thread of this 3x3 dispatch passes that check against the 4x4 destination, so the branch is translated and executed but does not discriminate: it cannot, because the writes it guards are the ones Metal would drop anyway. What the 3x3 dispatch into a 4x4 destination does establish is that the seven texels no thread writes come back exactly as authored, 0xabab -- a value the shift cannot produce, because anything shifted left by six ends in six zero bits. A dispatch that covered them, or an executor that did not honour an output texture's authored initial bytes, would answer 0 there instead; measured against the same case dispatched 4x4, where those seven texels do become 0.

`loop_free`: no loop, and the only calls are the two size queries, the read and the write. Both textures are single-channel `r16_uint`, so the three `undef` lanes of the written vector are not stored and the answer does not depend on what an undefined lane would contain.

name: collapse-an-accumulated-colour-normalisation-to-an-identity
rationale:
chromatic_transform normalises an accumulated colour by the weight it accumulated, so with `color1`, `color2` and `color3` all equal the normalisation is an identity and the mix chain that produces the weight cannot perturb the result -- which is what makes this kernel authorable at all.  Its per-sample jitter is `fract` of a product of four numbers near seventeen, magnified to six figures before the fraction is taken, so the mix parameter is not something a derivation can predict; every mix here is given equal endpoints instead, and `air.mix` at equal endpoints must return that endpoint however it is spelled.  The second `air.mix.v3f16` gets `saturate(2t - 1)` for a weight and the first gets `saturate(2t)`, so both saturating ends of the colour ramp are run.  The hash itself still executes: `air.fast_fmod.v3f32` and both `air.fast_fract` widths feed the parameter, and nothing in the module says the endpoints are equal, so no folding can remove them.

Everything the output does depend on is a power of two.  `sample_count` is 1, `fromZ` and `toZ` are 1, both angles are 0 and both shifts are zero, so the sample coordinate collapses to `(id + 0.5) / 16` -- the exact centre of texel `id` in a 16x16 texture, where the sampler's linear filter degenerates to a fetch.  `air.cos.f16(-0)` must be 1 and `air.sin.f16(-0)` must be -0 for that collapse to hold; either one wrong rotates every coordinate off its centre and the bilinear blend of four neighbours appears.  Each texel carries its largest channel in red or green, never in blue, and that maximum is an even power of two between 2^-4 and 2^4, so `air.fmax3.f16` picks a value whose `air.pow.f16(x, 0.5)` is exactly 2^(k/2) for any implementation of pow -- an exponent-halving that no rounding can reach.  The division that follows is by that power of two, and the final `air.mix.v4f16` blends the texel against the normalised triple with a weight of 0.5, which is exact because every difference it takes is a difference of powers of two inside binary16's eleven bits.  Alpha is the one lane where the two mix operands differ in kind: the first carries the texel's alpha, the second carries `pow`'s result, so a swapped mix would be visible there even where the colour lanes happen to agree.  `intensity`, the uniform at offset 0, is 12.5 and is never read; the struct's first member is a decoy for any decoder that starts at the buffer's base.

name: run-the-accumulation-loop-three-times-for-the-same-identity
rationale: The same collapse with `sample_count` = 3, which runs the accumulation loop three times and makes the normalisation divide 3*w by 3*w rather than w by w.  Every accumulated quantity is three times a power of two, which is exact in binary16, so the identity survives the loop -- but only if the loop actually ran three times: two or four iterations leave 2*w or 4*w in the denominator against the same numerator and every texel changes.  The mix parameter now advances by `1/half(3)` per iteration on top of the jitter, so the three iterations see three different weights and the equal-endpoint identity is asserted three times over rather than once.  The final blend weight is 0.25 instead of 0.5, so the two cases disagree on every texel and neither can be produced by the other's constants.

name: split-a-mask-radius-into-a-normalised-and-an-unnormalised-path
rationale:
`mask_enabled` is true here, which switches on a second entry path this kernel never takes otherwise: a thread whose distance from `maskCenter` exceeds `maskRadius` skips the accumulation loop entirely and samples the input once, unnormalised.  The mask distance is computed in binary16 from `2*half(uv) - 1` against a centre of zero and a radius of 0.5, and both sides are exact -- the squared distance is a multiple of 1/256 and the radius squared is 0.25, which by a parity argument (an odd square is 1 mod 8, so a sum of two is 2 mod 8, and 64 is 0 mod 8) no thread can hit exactly, so no thread sits on the comparison's boundary.  52 of the 256 threads fall inside and take the loop.

The two paths are told apart by giving the third colour component the value zero.  On the loop path the accumulated blue weight is zero, the `air.fmax` floor of 0x0011 replaces it, and blue divides to exactly zero; on the direct path no normalisation happens and blue keeps the texel's own value.  Every texel's largest channel is red or green, so both paths agree on which channel `air.fmax3.f16` selects and on the `air.pow.f16` exponent halving that follows -- the blue lane is the only difference, which is what makes the branch readable rather than merely taken.  A translation that lost the mask predicate, or inverted it, moves 52 or 204 texels between the two shapes.

The one-bin histogram parameters force every active scalar lane to bin zero, and the poisoned counter makes the bounded global-atomic write observable byte-exactly.

rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: msl-4-1-atomics-on-thread-memory
rationale: One threadgroup of 8 threads over one zeroed 768-byte buffer (DESIGN D301). Thread t runs every MSL 4.1 atomic on its own thread atomics of uint, int, float, and bool (air.atomic.private.*) and writes 24 words at out[24 t], as the fixture's header documents: with x = t * 0x01010101 + 3, s = int(x) - 100, and f = float(t) * 0.5, [0] x; [1] x + 5; [2] x + 3; [3] A = (x + 3) & 0xf0f0f0f0; [4] B = A | 0x0101; [5] C = B ^ 0xffff; [6] D = min(C, 0x1000); [7] max(D, 0x800); [8] 1 and [9] 77; [10] 0 and [11] 88; [12] 88; [13] s; [14] min(s, -7); [15] 3; [16] 2; [17] f, [18] f + 1.25, [19] f + 0.5, [20] -2.5 (bits); [21] x & 1; [22] 1; [23] 88. No other thread can reach a thread's memory, so the words are exact in any schedule. Loop-free.

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat-16-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (offset 0, 64 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[n][k] (row stride w_ld = 48 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in bfloat and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the bfloat inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-bfloat

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-three-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 23 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-two linked _uber_clear bodies. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: read-a-row-through-a-buffer-address-round-trip
rationale: Reads a struct through a pointer that only exists as an INTEGER in between: `ptrtoint` the bound buffer, add the host's byte offset, `inttoptr` back, index. That is the shape Apple's DilateFilter4 and ErodeFilter4 use to reach their structuring element, and it is the only shape in which the address of a descriptor-bound buffer is arithmetic rather than a pointer. Logical SPIR-V has no pointer address, so the integer itself must stay folded; what has to survive is which buffer it names and how far in. Buffer 0 holds two decoy rows of 0xFFFF followed by eight payload rows (i+1, i+10, i+20) as ushorts, and buffer 1 says byte_offset = 12, which is exactly the two decoy rows. Each of the eight threads reads row gid past that offset and packs the three members into disjoint bytes, so every member is separately visible in the answer: thread gid must write (gid+1) | (gid+10)<<8 | (gid+20)<<16. The three answers are all distinct. A lost address reads zero and every word is 0; a lost offset reads the decoy rows and word 0 is 0xFFFFFFFF; a correct read gives 0x140a01 upward. The 6-byte row also crosses the 4-byte word grid on every odd index, so the sub-word extraction is exercised at all three phases rather than only at zero.

name: read-through-a-merge-of-two-differently-declared-buffers
rationale: Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value that can be either of two descriptors, so a pointer merged from two DISTINCT device buffers has to be replayed in the VALUE domain: one load per arm and a select of the results. This merges buffers whose DECLARED element widths differ -- a `uchar` buffer viewed as words and a `uint` buffer -- because that is the shape the replay derives its load type from, and the two arms derive it from different declarations. The byte buffer holds 1000..1007 as little-endian words and the word buffer holds 2000..2007, so every value names its arm: an arm swap moves a result by exactly 1000. Odd lanes take the byte view and even lanes the word buffer, so both arms run in one dispatch and an inverted condition moves every row. The merge is read TWICE at two different indices, `gid` and `gid ^ 7`, because a replay that is correct for one consumer is not evidence about a second: the second index runs backwards, so a suffix applied to the wrong arm, or an index taken off the wrong consumer, gives a value that is neither 1000 + gid nor 2000 + gid. Every value is exact in u32, and the 0xCD fill is fully overwritten.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seven
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 7 and receives exact float4 zero from all six linked _uber_clear bodies. A nine-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: group-a-three-term-product-the-way-its-flag-run-says
rationale: Device evidence that an emitted module states the association order its AIR states. Metal decides its float relaxations from the module's math mode and the expression's precise-ness; SPIR-V has no equivalent module state, so a permission LLVM withheld has to travel on the instruction. The emitter used to spell that as NoContraction, which forbids fusing a multiply into an add and leaves REASSOCIATION permitted -- less than the AIR says, and MoltenVK's own fast-math default is on. 437 of the 14579 corpus sources carry a three-term association chain no instruction of which is marked fast or reassoc. Both multiplies here carry an EMPTY flag run, and the fixture ships the Metal half as a hand-written .air.ll for exactly that reason: newLibraryWithSource compiles a .metal with Metal's DEFAULT fast math mode, which would let the oracle regroup the very product under test. a and b are both 1 + 2^-23, the smallest float above one, and c is 3. In source order a*b is 1 + 2^-22 + 2^-46, which rounds to exactly 1 + 2^-22, and three times that is 3 + 2^-22 + 2^-21 -- exact, because the ulp at 3 is 2^-22 -- giving 3.0000007152557373 (0x40400003). Regrouped, b*c is 3 + 3*2^-23, which is 1.5 ulp above 3 and rounds to even at 3 + 2^-21, and a times that is 3.0000009536743164 (0x40400004). The two orders are one ulp apart, so the single output word names which grouping ran, and nothing else can move it: there is no add to fuse into, no division to reciprocate, every input is exact, and one thread means nothing races.

name: linked-single-offset-copy
rationale: One invocation selects the rank-one, one-element path. Zero enabled offset dimensions avoid indirect array access, zero strides address element zero in both direct buffers, and the linked secondary prefix is the exact retained zero-offset implementation. The kernel copies the authored 32-bit input into the poisoned output.

name: a-signed-integer-sample-reaches-the-attachment-unrounded
rationale:
A fragment whose return type is `int4` and whose attachment is a signed-integer render target. `passes::stage_output::bitcast_for_store` is what puts the returned value into the attachment when the two SPIR-V types differ, and it does so with `OpBitcast` -- the BITS pass through, they are not converted numerically. Seven corpus sources reach that function and no authored case did; measured with per-function coverage against every cased source, this one reaches it and it is the only unverified function it reaches.

The distinction a bitcast has to survive is a numeric round trip, so every one of the sixty-four integers in the answer is chosen to be destroyed by one. Each texel is (2^24 + i, -(2^24 + i), INT_MAX - i, INT_MIN + i) for its index i. The first two are the smallest magnitudes binary32 cannot represent exactly, so a float round trip rounds every odd one to its even neighbour; the last two are one saturation step from the signed limits, which a float-to-int convert clamps. A lowering that converted instead of reinterpreting moves 48 of the 64 words, and one that reinterpreted through the WRONG signedness moves the negative ones.

The sample is `air.sample_texture_2d.s.v4i32` through a runtime sampler this case authors as nearest, normalized, clamp-to-edge over a 4x4 texture the size of the 4x4 target, so each fragment reads exactly one texel and no filtering is involved -- integer textures cannot be filtered anyway. The `texCoord` varying is the harness's `(uv.x, uv.y)`, and at pixel (px, py) of a 4x4 target that is ((px+0.5)/4, 1-(py+0.5)/4), which under this sampler is texel (px, 3-py): the y axis is mirrored and the x axis is direct. Pixel centres land on texel centres, half a texel from any boundary, which is 2000 times the measured end-to-end deviation of an interpolated varying, so the selected texel cannot move.

So the answer is the texture with its rows reversed, and Metal saying so is a check of both the bitcast and the orientation. The attachment starts filled with 0xab bytes, which is -1414812757 in every lane and appears nowhere in the texture.

`loop_free`: one sample and a return, no branch. One fullscreen triangle, one instance.

name: ask-a-runtime-selected-texture-four-questions
rationale: An OpSelect on an image value is not valid SPIR-V, so a runtime-chosen texture handle has to be pushed DOWN through every pure use: each question is asked of BOTH arms and the RESULTS are selected. This asks four questions of one select -- a size query, a second size query on the other axis, a fetch, and a sample through OpSampledImage -- because the four take different paths and a rule that pushes the select through one of them is not evidence about the others. The two textures differ in BOTH extent and content, so every answer names its arm: a is 4x2 holding 100 + x + 10y, b is 2x4 holding 200 + x + 10y. Odd lanes take a and even lanes take b, so both arms run in one dispatch and an inverted condition swaps every row. Width and height are asked separately because a transposed extent (4,2) vs (2,4) is exactly what a wrong arm looks like. The fetch reads texel (1,0), which is in range for both, and the sample is nearest with clamp_to_edge at (0.8, 0.3) -- floor(0.8*4)=3 and floor(0.3*2)=0 on a, floor(0.8*2)=1 and floor(0.3*4)=1 on b -- so the two arms land on DIFFERENT texels and neither coordinate is near a rounding boundary. Every value is a small integer exact in f32, and the 0xAB fill in the output buffer is fully overwritten, so a dropped store is visible as a NaN rather than a zero.

name: front-facing-half2-location-one
